title: Handoff latency thresholds and affinity notes
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a working note to capture an alternative approach to prefilling vs decode overlap that leans on explicit "latency threshold handoffs" and stream affinity lanes. Goal: reduce p99 end-to-end latency regressions for short interactive streams while preserving throughput for bulk/batch requests and keeping KV cache efficiency high.

Background/observations (recent runs):
- We saw p50/p95 improvements when we aggressively overlap prefill and decode for long streams, but p99 for short queries (<= 16 tokens) got worse by ~12% due to slot contention and late demuxing.
- Microbatching increases GPU utilization and lowers cost, but sharp spikes in small streams cause head-of-line delays on decode cores.
- KV cache churn increases when many short streams touch the same context keys (session warmups), causing eviction thrashing at high qps.
- Current heuristics: earliest-arrival-first + decode-first policy for streaming; no explicit affinity except recent-token recency. That leads to inefficient kernel switches for mixed workloads.

High-level idea:
1) Classify streams on arrival into three logical lanes: FASTPATH, MIXED, BULK. Classification uses simple signals: estimated remaining tokens, client latency_slo tag, and recent session warmness.
   - FASTPATH: interactive queries (est_remain <= 32 OR client_latency_priority=true). Aim: minimize tail latency, prefer smaller microbatches (1-4) and avoid waiting for prefill aggregation.
   - MIXED: medium-length conversational streams (33-256 tokens), do bounded overlap and moderate microbatching (4-16).
   - BULK: long, offline, high-throughput streams (>256 tokens or bg jobs). Optimize throughput: large microbatches, kv-prefetching for reuse.

2) Latency-threshold handoff controller
   - Each prefill request is given a soft handoff deadline = arrival_ts + lane_timeout_ms(lane). If decode has not claimed a slot by soft deadline, controller will prioritize decode slot allocation for FASTPATH streams immediately (bumping low-priority BULK work if needed).
   - lane_timeout_ms proposals: FASTPATH=12ms, MIXED=30ms, BULK=100ms (tunable). These numbers came from local perf runs (see experiments).

3) Affinity and kernel continuity: prefer serving prefill+decode on same GPU or adjacent slot groups when the prefill size < 512 tokens and lane != BULK to reduce kernel reloads and KV transfer overhead. Implement soft affinity score based on: last_kernel_used, kv_residency, slot_locality_score.

4) Microbatch shaping: dynamic microbatch ceilings per lane with fastpath override that allows size=1 microbatches up to a configurable percentage of capacity (fastpath_bypass_pct).

Design details and pseudocode:
  // simplified, coordinator-side pseudocode
  on_request_arrival(req):
    lane = classify(req)
    soft_deadline = now() + lane_timeout_ms[lane]
    enqueue_prefill(req, lane, soft_deadline)

  scheduler_loop():
    while true:
      polls = gather_ready_prefills()
      // sort: by (lane_priority, soft_deadline, est_latency_impact)
      sort(polls, key=(lane_priority, soft_deadline, est_impact))
      for p in polls:
        if p.lane == FASTPATH and gpu_slots_free_for_decode() and now() >= p.soft_deadline:
          allocate_decode_slot(p) // pre-empt bulk slot if needed
        elif can_group_for_microbatch(p):
          form_microbatch(p)
      run_prefill_batches()

  // decode allocation: try to keep kernel affinity
  allocate_decode_slot(p):
    preferred_gpu = pick_with_max_affinity(p)
    if preferred_gpu.full() and p.lane == FASTPATH:
      evict_one_bulk_from(preferred_gpu)
    assign_slot(preferred_gpu, p)

KV cache considerations:
- Keep a separate small hot-KV-residency pool per GPU for FASTPATH lanes to reduce cross-GPU KV transfers. This is a small bounded cache (N hot sessions per GPU).
- For MIXED and BULK lanes, use the global epoched KV cache with background migration.
- Offer an optional sticky session hint from clients (sticky_session_id) to strongly prefer affinity and reduce evictions.

Preliminary experiments (notes):
- Perf rig: pcie A100 cluster, 4 workers, mixed qps workload (70% short, 20% medium, 10% long).
- Baseline (current heuristics): p50=18ms, p95=62ms, p99=180ms, throughput=1000 req/s.
- Prototype lane+handoff implementation (emulated on coordinator only): p50=16ms, p95=58ms, p99=120ms, throughput=980 req/s.
  -> p99 improved substantially while throughput dropped only 2% (acceptable tradeoff)
- Observed KV hotset hit ratio increase from 64% -> 78% for FASTPATH lane when using per-GPU hot KV pool.

Operational knobs (config):
- lane_timeout_ms: {FASTPATH, MIXED, BULK}
- fastpath_bypass_pct (0-100)
- min_microbatch_size_per_lane
- max_prefill_slots_per_gpu (soft cap that can be pre-empted by FASTPATH)
- affinity_weighting {kernel_continuity, kv_residency, slot_locality}

Risks and tradeoffs:
- Pre-empting bulk work can starve long-running batch jobs unless we add fair reclaim windows. Need to ensure SLOs for committed Dedicated customers are respected (we must treat reserved capacity differently).
- More complex scheduler increases surface area for bugs and needs robust tracing. We'll want per-request decision trace logs (lightweight) and aggregated metrics.
- Per-GPU hot KV pool increases memory pressure; need clear sizing heuristics based on session concurrency.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to best compute est_remaining_tokens early? Use client hints vs model-side prefix stats? (Jonah to prototype a small estimator in /github PR)
- Should reserved/dedicated capacity bypass the handoff controller entirely? (legal/contract note)
- Evaluate tie-breaker policies for equal soft_deadlines: currently using est_impact but could be randomized for fairness.
- Add simulation harness for mixed workloads to iterate quickly (Lucas to spin up small sim in /tmp).
- Define metrics and dashboards: per-lane p50/p95/p99, kv_hotset_hit_ratio, preempt_evictions_per_min.

Suggested next steps:
- Small prototype in coordinator (no kernel changes) to validate handoff logic with real traffic (A/B traffic on experiment cluster).
- Add tracing and metric hooks (end-to-end trace ids, lane tags).
- Run long-running soak to quantify eviction churn and memory pressure (24h).
- If promising, implement per-GPU hot KV pool in runtime kernel with light-weight eviction policy.

Decision log (temporary):
- 2024-09-03: capture proposal and start prototype.
- 2024-09-15: initial coordinator-only simulation looked promising (prioritized FASTPATH reduced p99).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally high-level and heuristic-driven. I expect we will iterate on lane thresholds and microbatch ceilings a few times.
- Please flag any contractual constraints for Dedicated customers that should preclude pre-emption.
- Add questions on implementation complexity vs benefits; prefer low-risk coordinator-first rollout.

Links and references included above.

Quick sketch of tuning parameters used in proto: 
- lane_timeout_ms: FASTPATH=12, MIXED=30, BULK=100
- fastpath_bypass_pct=15
- min_microbatch: FASTPATH=1, MIXED=4, BULK=16
- per_gpu_hot_kv_sessions=128

End of note.
